prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: production RGBA sprite sheet of exterior buildings for an overhead 16-bit RPG, same detailed warm hand-painted pixel-art village style as the earlier town screenshots. Primary request: buildings must have REAL visible architectural depth rather than looking like a flat pasted frontal photograph. Exactly FOUR separate small town buildings in a strict regular 2 columns by 2 rows grid, square equal cells on a square canvas. Top left compact two-storey home with terracotta gable roof; top right small shop with ochre tile roof and a short awning; bottom left welcoming inn with broad reddish-brown gable roof; bottom right stone-and-timber archive with muted moss-green roof. Every building uses the SAME three-quarter top-down RPG camera: front wall facing down toward player, substantial RIGHT wall visible as a receding depth plane with small side windows, broad roof top surface with ridge, eaves overhang casting a dark line, raised masonry foundation with tiny front doorstep. Front door centered at BOTTOM FRONT of each building, consistent ground-contact pivot at bottom center of each cell, generous empty transparent margins. All sprites similar physical scale and height, no labels or signs with text, no people, no trees or floor islands attached, no rectangular backdrop, no perspective horizon. Rich hand-placed pixel detail, cream plaster, warm exposed timber, masonry stones and ceramic roof tiles, readable crisp edges and subtle directional shade; cozy original first-chapter town identity, not desert and not neon cyberpunk. Real transparent background with alpha, not checkerboard. Avoid frontal orthographic flat facade, avoid photorealistic image, avoid 3D glossy rendering, avoid dramatic isometric diamond foundation, avoid ground shadow baked as a big opaque slab. Runtime will add the footprint shadows and public shop labels.
